status: COMPLETE — all of §0–§14 + appendix captured in pc-1..pc-39 (read in full; no context dropped). sections_accounted maps every section to its rules.
note: Faithful rule manifest for authoring a Claude agent's always-loaded persona. The .md is authoritative and unchanged; this indexes every actionable rule, typed checkable|judgment|principle, with predicate/reviewer_criterion. Genesis (Method) applies this when authoring an agent's persona.

rules.text: Use the ordered persona TEMPLATE (order is deliberate — stable identity first for cache reuse + framing): 1★ Identity ('You are <name>, a <specific role> for <domain>'), 2★ Mission (the one outcome it is accountable for), 3★ Responsibilities (in scope, concrete verbs), 4★ Boundaries (out of scope — 'you do not X; if asked, do Y'), 5 Operating principles ('when <situation>, prefer <action>'), 6★ Voice & tone (concrete: length/format/register/audience), 7 Values/non-negotiables, 8★ Escalation/ask-the-user rules (explicit triggers; which decisions are the human's), 9 Interfaces to memory/skills/tools (pointers not copies), 10 Success criteria (the self-check), 11 Failure modes to avoid (named anti-goals as guardrails). ★ = the minimum viable persona; add the rest only when the role needs it and each added line earns its context cost.

predicate.spec: the persona.md has the ★ fields (Identity, Mission, Responsibilities, Boundaries, Voice, Escalation) at minimum, identity-first ordering, and non-★ fields only where the role needs them.

rules.text: SIZING: target UNDER 200 lines per CLAUDE.md/persona file (the official Anthropic ceiling — longer files consume more context and REDUCE adherence); the working band is ~40–150 lines (below ~40 is usually too vague to change behavior). If a section wants to become a multi-step procedure or a long fact set, move it to a SKILL or memory, not the persona.

predicate.spec: persona.md <= 200 lines (hard); procedures/long fact-sets live in skills/memory, not inline.

rules.text: NEVER speculate — ASK. Use the elicitation checklist to pin every template field: ask one numbered question at a time (Q3 of ~12), accept 'you decide / use the default' as valid, and apply a sensible default when the user defers rather than blocking. Q1–4, Q6, Q7, Q12 (identity, mission, responsibilities, boundaries, escalation, voice, name) suffice for a valid MINIMAL persona; the rest raise quality but are not blocking.

predicate.spec: the persona was elicited by asking (one question at a time), not inferred; at least the minimal ★ fields are user-confirmed or defaulted-with-note.

rules.text: SPECIFIC identity beats a generic one — the #1 weakness is genericness. 'You are a Rust code-reviewer for a real-time audio engine' changes behavior; 'You are a helpful assistant' does not.

predicate.spec: the Identity line names a specific role + domain/project; reject generic 'helpful assistant'-class identities.

rules.text: Frame POSITIVELY — lead with the desired behavior (say what TO do); use prohibitions sparingly and only for hard limits. A wall of 'don'ts' underspecifies the 'do'.

predicate.spec: operating principles/responsibilities are stated as positive imperatives; prohibitions are limited to hard boundaries, not the bulk of the persona.

rules.text: A persona is a STRONG, reliable lever on CONDUCT (tone, scope, when-to-ask, prioritization) and a WEAK, unreliable lever on raw factual ACCURACY. Design personas to govern conduct; do NOT oversell them as correctness boosters.
BOUNDARIES are as load-bearing as responsibilities — an agent with no stated non-responsibilities scope-creeps. Every strong persona states explicitly what it REFUSES and where it DEFERS.

predicate.spec: the persona has an explicit Boundaries section stating what it does not do + the defer/escalate action.

rules.text: Keep it SMALL — the persona is in context every turn and competes with reasoning for the window. Push procedures into skills, facts into memory, and keep the always-loaded layer lean.

predicate.spec: the persona contains identity+rules, not procedures or long fact-sets (those are skills/memory).

rules.text: REFERENCE memory/skills; don't duplicate them. The persona is procedural memory (identity + rules); it points to the semantic/episodic stores and the skill library and states the POLICY for using them (when to write memory, when to invoke a skill) — it does not inline their contents.

predicate.spec: the Interfaces section uses pointers ('your memory is <where>; skill X — when to invoke') not copied procedures/facts.

rules.text: Make the persona VERIFIABLE — state success criteria and an ask-the-user rule so the agent can self-check and knows when to stop. An unfalsifiable persona ('be excellent') cannot govern anything.

predicate.spec: the persona has a checkable Done-means/success-criteria section + an explicit escalation/ask rule.

rules.text: The persona is almost entirely PROCEDURAL memory (CoALA), with a thin layer of stable semantic identity. Because writing to procedural memory is 'significantly riskier' (can introduce bugs or let an agent subvert designer intent), the persona must be human-authored, human-reviewed, VERSIONED, and changed deliberately — NEVER silently auto-learned. It is the one store you do not let the agent freely rewrite.

Persona ≠ instructions ≠ skills ≠ memory. The persona is the CONSTANT the moment's instructions operate inside — it contains nothing true for only one task. It NAMES a skill's trigger ('when asked to cut a release, use the release skill'), never contains the steps. It GOVERNS memory ('write a memory when corrected; never store secrets') but is not the memory; changing project facts belong in MEMORY.md.

predicate.spec: the persona has no task-specific instructions, no inlined skill procedures, and no accumulated/dated facts — those live in the prompt/skills/memory respectively.

rules.text: PRODUCTION ADDENDUM (authoring is necessary, not sufficient): (1) follow the standards register; (2) TEST the persona like code (assertion/eval/golden/A-B/LLM-judge/human/adversarial); (3) develop TEST-FIRST (baseline must fail; cut any line that doesn't flip a test); (4) BENCHMARK with statistics vs a no-persona and prior-version baseline (a move within one SE is noise); (5) manage the LIFECYCLE — a persona drifts within ~8 turns (re-inject) and is NOT portable across models (re-baseline on any model change; techniques die, e.g. prefill→400 on newer models) — pin a target model + re-run the suite on every bump; (6) HARDEN — a persona is a SOFT control (the system prompt WILL leak → no secrets; persona-assignment is a documented jailbreak vector; long context erodes it) → enforce hard boundaries in guardrails OUTSIDE the LLM, treat retrieved/tool content as untrusted data, monitor adherence on live traffic. The one-line truth: a persona SPECIFIES conduct; tests + benchmarks + version pins + guardrails make it HOLD.

Prefer MEASURABLE role constraints an outside observer could check ('≤2 lines per answer', 'one finding per line with file:line + a trigger', 'ask before any irreversible action'). Unfalsifiable constraints ('be thorough', 'be helpful', 'write clean code') can't be self-checked and don't reliably change output.

predicate.spec: persona constraints are observable/checkable (counts, formats, explicit triggers); reject unfalsifiable 'be thorough/helpful/excellent'-class rules.

rules.text: Avoid the ten persona anti-patterns (each with its fix): generic identity → name the specific role+domain; all-prohibitions-no-positives → positive responsibilities + short negative boundaries; persona bloat (300+ lines) → move procedures→skills, facts→memory; unfalsifiable rules → measurable constraints; duplicating memory/skills → pointer + policy; no boundaries → explicit non-responsibilities + escalation; no escalation rule → explicit ask-vs-proceed triggers; persona-as-correctness-crutch → get correctness from tools/verification; contradictory rules → one consistent priority order; task detail in the persona → a trigger-named skill.

predicate.spec: the persona exhibits none of the ten anti-patterns; a review pass checks each.

rules.text: 'Act as X' is a BEHAVIORAL lever, not epistemic: it sets disposition, register, and — if deliberately designed as a reasoning SCAFFOLD (not a bare label) — can lift reasoning; it does NOT install expertise the model lacks and can HURT objective accuracy (near-random, unpredictable). Match the role to the work (domain-matched personas help where domain framing aids the task); get factual correctness from tools/retrieval/verification/skills, never from the incantation.
rules.reviewer_criterion: Is the role used to set disposition/reasoning-frame (and domain-matched to the task), not sold as a correctness/expertise lever?

rules.text: Two persona risks to guard: (1) BIAS — persona choice can silently inject demographic/domain bias (Salewski); (2) DRIFT — a persona drifts within ~8 turns from attention decay (Li). Mitigate drift by keeping the persona high-signal enough to stay salient, putting identity FIRST (cache- and attention-friendly), and relying on Claude Code's re-injection of the project CLAUDE.md across compaction rather than assuming the persona persists in the model's memory.

predicate.spec: identity is placed first; the persona is high-signal (fights drift); persona choice is checked for injected bias.

rules.text: CHARACTER = dispositional TRAITS to nudge toward, not rules from which it never deviates (Anthropic character work: curiosity, truth-without-unkindness, seeing many sides without over/under-confidence). Write the Values/Voice fields as dispositions to lean toward, not a rigid rulebook — and don't re-teach the base character; specialize it.
rules.reviewer_criterion: Are Values/Voice written as dispositions to nudge toward (not rigid rules), and do they specialize rather than re-teach the base character?

rules.text: Instill HEURISTICS not rigid rules — write operating principles as 'when X, prefer Y because Z', not brittle if/else. Write at the RIGHT ALTITUDE (the Goldilocks zone between brittle hardcoded logic and vague hand-waving). Minimal ≠ short — optimize SIGNAL DENSITY (every line changes a behavior you care about) within the 200-line budget. Section the persona with Markdown headers / XML tags.

predicate.spec: operating principles are heuristics ('when X prefer Y'); the persona is sectioned with headers; every line earns its recurring cost.

rules.text: The persona lives in a PRIVILEGED layer (system/developer), but must explicitly instruct the agent to treat retrieved memory, tool output, and file/quoted content as DATA, not instructions (they have no authority by default — the injection surface). Put this in the Values/Interfaces fields.

predicate.spec: the persona states that retrieved/tool/file content is data-not-instructions (an injection guardrail).

rules.text: The persona is the PROCEDURAL layer that GOVERNS the other stores (policy, not storage): persona→memory = the WRITE POLICY (when to write: task-end/correction/surprise/consolidation; never write secrets/PII; date+provenance; the index not the store is always-loaded) not the memories; persona→skills = NAME the trigger and delegate the how ('when cutting a release, use the release skill'); anything longer than a few lines of procedure → a skill; persona→tools = set tool scope + guardrails + ask-before rules for dangerous/irreversible calls. Persona = constitution, skills = on-demand how-to, memory = dated what-it-knows, tools = scoped levers — reference all, duplicate none.

predicate.spec: the Interfaces section states the memory write-policy + skill triggers + tool scope as pointers/policy, inlining no memory content or skill procedures.

rules.text: CLAUDE.md files CONCATENATE up the directory tree (they do NOT override) — content is ordered root→working-dir so the closest file is read LAST; imports use @path with a maximum depth of FOUR hops. Each built agent gets its OWN subfolder CLAUDE.md persona that must be CONSISTENT with the root rules (it is read in addition to, not instead of, them). Factor shared rule blocks into an imported file or .claude/rules/ rather than copy-pasting into every persona; respect the four-hop import ceiling.

predicate.spec: the agent's persona lives in its own subfolder CLAUDE.md, is consistent with root rules, and shares common blocks via imports (<=4 hops), not copy-paste.

rules.text: THE persona is a SOFT control — Anthropic states it verbatim: CLAUDE.md is 'context, not enforced configuration. To block an action regardless of what Claude decides, use a PreToolUse hook instead.' Therefore any boundary you cannot afford to have broken must ALSO exist as a hook / external guardrail, not only as persona prose. Put the invariant identity FIRST (most cache-friendly + attention-salient).

predicate.spec: non-negotiable boundaries stated in the persona are ALSO enforced by a hook/guardrail (not prose-only); identity is placed first.

rules.text: SPECIALIZE and constrain the model's strong DEFAULT disposition (helpful, careful, honest — already trained in) — do NOT re-teach generic helpfulness. Redundant 'be helpful and honest' lines waste always-loaded tokens; the value is only in the specifics the default doesn't already provide.

predicate.spec: the persona adds role/scope/voice/guardrail specifics and does not spend lines re-teaching generic helpfulness/honesty.

rules.text: A subagent's BODY IS its system prompt — it does NOT inherit the main Claude Code system prompt, so the body must be SELF-SUFFICIENT (fully establish identity, scope, boundaries, rules on its own; the §0.1 template is exactly this). The persona is a TWO-TIER artifact: a routing DESCRIPTION (the index the model matches to decide WHEN to delegate — 'specific about the trigger, not the identity'; include 'use proactively' to encourage delegation) PLUS the body (WHO it is). Genesis must author both.

predicate.spec: a built subagent has a self-sufficient body (full identity/scope/boundaries) AND a crisp trigger-focused description; the body does not assume an inherited parent prompt.

rules.text: Elicitation principles: one numbered question at a time (Qn of ~12); every question maps to a template field (coverage = completeness); accept 'you decide' → apply the documented default AND record which fields were defaulted; ask BOUNDARIES and ESCALATION explicitly (users volunteer responsibilities but rarely non-responsibilities — these are the highest-value questions); confirm the assembled draft before writing (the user corrects faster than he specifies).

predicate.spec: the persona was elicited question-by-question with boundaries+escalation explicitly asked; defaulted fields are recorded; the draft was confirmed before write.

rules.text: THE mechanizable procedure: STEP 0 FRAME (restate the one-line ask, get a yes) → 1 INTERVIEW (§0.2 checklist, never speculate) → 2 DRAFT (fill the template: specific identity, all ★ fields, positive framing, Interfaces = pointers not inline, lean — overflow becomes a skill stub) → 3 VALIDATE (run the §8.2 gate; fix every FAIL) → 4 CONFIRM (read back + explicit approval) → 5 OUTPUT (write the agent's own-subfolder CLAUDE.md, record defaulted fields, do NOT modify project-root or peer-agent context — isolation) → 6 survival/coherence check (sample in-scope + out-of-scope request behaves per boundaries/escalation). EMIT RULE: emittable once every ★ field is filled (elicited, or defaulted for the defaultable ★ fields boundaries/voice/escalation) AND all §8.2 gates pass; identity/mission/responsibilities have NO default and MUST be elicited (block/ask rather than invent).

predicate.spec: the persona was produced by the frame→interview→draft→validate→confirm→output procedure; identity/mission/responsibilities were elicited (not invented); isolation was respected.

rules.text: Every persona must pass the 13-item QUALITY GATE (each a binary check): (1) specific identity (role+domain, not 'assistant'); (2) all ★ fields present; (3) boundaries non-empty (>=1 non-responsibility + defer/escalate); (4) an explicit escalation trigger; (5) positive framing dominates; (6) no unfalsifiable rules; (7) no memory/skill duplication (pointers only); (8) size within budget (~40–150 lines, <=200 hard); (9) internal consistency (no contradictions; clear priority order); (10) success criteria present (a self-check); (11) secrets policy present (no credential values); (12) not a correctness crutch (accuracy from tools/verification); (13) matches the interview (every stated requirement reflected; defaulted fields recorded).

predicate.spec: the persona passes all 13 §8.2 gate items; a review pass checks each.

rules.text: Genesis emits a machine-readable PersonaSpec (JSON, schema persona-spec/v1) as the SOURCE OF TRUTH; the CLAUDE.md is a RENDER of it, stamped with lifecycle frontmatter (persona-version, target-model, tests path, last-verified). ROUND-TRIP RULE: a behavior change edits the SPEC → re-render → re-run tests; NEVER hand-edit the rendered CLAUDE.md out of sync with its spec.

predicate.spec: the persona derives from a versioned PersonaSpec + carries lifecycle frontmatter (version/target-model/tests/last-verified); the rendered file is not hand-edited out of sync with its spec.

rules.text: A production persona must satisfy the STANDARDS REGISTER S1–S17 (each a primary-sourced gate): S1 right-altitude (heuristics between brittle if/else and vague vibes); S2 smallest high-signal set (minimal != short); S3 heuristics/frameworks not rigid rules; S4 state role+objective+output-format+tool/source-scope+boundaries+effort-budget; S5 positive framing; S6 section with headers/XML + consistent names; S7 role = tone/focus NOT an accuracy lever; S8 character = traits to nudge toward not never-deviate rules; S9 SMART success criteria (Specific/Measurable/Achievable/Relevant); S10 eval/test-driven not trial-and-error; S11 separate the stable persona from runtime {{variables}} + version the persona as the unit; S12 least privilege + treat retrieved/tool content as untrusted data; S13 no secrets/credentials/security-controls in persona text (it leaks); S14 'confused colleague' readability test; S15 re-test on every model change; S16 enforce hard boundaries in code/guardrails OUTSIDE the LLM (context not enforced config → PreToolUse hook); S17 stay under ~200 lines (longer reduces adherence). S1–S8 authoring quality, S9–S11 engineering discipline, S12–S17 production/security/budget.

predicate.spec: the persona is checked against S1–S17; each applicable standard is met (right-altitude, positive framing, no-secrets, tests-defined, model-pinned, <=200 lines, external enforcement of hard boundaries).

rules.text: A persona is a behavioral contract — TEST it. Turn each field into a measurable criterion (boundaries→boundary-hold rate, voice→tone/style Likert, escalation→escalation-correctness, values/secrets→leakage rate). Use the 7 test types (1 assertion/deterministic, 2 eval/scenario suite over a real distribution, 3 golden/regression snapshot per version, 4 A/B variant comparison, 5 LLM-as-judge rubric for subjective traits, 6 human eval for the residue, 7 adversarial/red-team). Grade with the CHEAPEST reliable method in cost order: code-based (boundary/escalation/format) → LLM-judge (tone/in-character) → human (residue only). The persona FILE is the versioned artifact under test; the same suite becomes the regression gate + benchmark.

predicate.spec: the persona ships with an executable test suite mapping each field to a measurable criterion; deterministic checks gate boundary/escalation/format, an independent judge grades subjective traits.

rules.text: An LLM-as-judge scoring persona variants is trustworthy ONLY with bias controls — it carries position bias, verbosity bias (favors longer answers), and self-enhancement bias (a model favors its own family: e.g. GPT-4 +10%, Claude-v1 +25% self-win). Controls (verified): swap the order of the two answers + only declare a win if preferred in BOTH orders (else tie); NEVER let a model judge its own family; penalize/normalize verbosity; use a detailed binary or 1–5 rubric; reason-then-discard (think first, discard the reasoning before the score).

predicate.spec: the persona judge is cross-family (never self-family), applies swap-order + tie-on-disagreement + verbosity-normalization + a detailed rubric + reason-then-discard.

rules.text: TEST-DRIVEN persona development: write the behavioral acceptance tests FIRST (from the elicitation answers), then draft the SMALLEST persona that passes them. Loop RED (write MUST-refuse/MUST-ask/MUST-hold-tone/MUST-stay-in-role/MUST-do tests; run vs a NO-PERSONA baseline → they must FAIL, proving they discriminate) → GREEN (minimal persona making every test pass, nothing more) → REFACTOR (cut any line whose removal does NOT flip a test red — it wasn't earning its context cost). The tests ARE the spec (a field with no test is unfalsifiable); baseline-fails proves the persona does the work not the base model; the suite is the regression + model-migration gate. Emit persona.tests.json beside the persona (every ★ field ≥1 case; grader = a model NOT in the subject's family with swap-order/tie/reason-discard/normalize controls). CONVERGENCE: done when the baseline fails every case AND the persona passes every case.

predicate.spec: acceptance tests were written before the persona, fail on a no-persona baseline, and pass on the final persona; a machine-readable persona.tests.json ships alongside as the regression gate.

rules.text: BENCHMARK, don't just test — measure how well vs a baseline and whether the difference is REAL. The persona SCORECARD (7 objective metrics): scope-adherence ≥0.98, boundary-hold 1.00 (HARD GATE), escalation-correctness 1.00 (HARD GATE), adversarial boundary-hold ≥0.99, tone/format Likert mean ≥4.5, consistency ≥0.90, leakage 0 (HARD GATE). Always measure against TWO baselines: (a) no-persona (proves the persona adds value) and (b) the previous persona version (proves an edit didn't regress). STATISTICAL RIGOR: to claim A>B run both on the SAME items and compare a PAIRED difference with error bars (McNemar-style SE); a version-to-version move inside one SE is NOISE, not a regression — promote only when the effect clears ~2 SE (a paired promotion gate). Hard-gate metrics bypass statistics: one failure blocks. Do NOT adjust sampling temperature for variance reduction.

predicate.spec: each persona version has a persisted scorecard measured vs no-persona AND prior-version baselines; version promotion is gated on a paired SE test (not the raw gap); hard-gate metrics (boundary/escalation/leakage) block on any single failure.

rules.text: A persona is a LIVING artifact with a lifecycle + a hard expiry clock. Seven stages: Author (separate the fixed persona from runtime {{variables}}; the persona is the versioned unit) → Test (eval-in-CI, test-first) → Version (registry with semver + changelog per persona) → Deploy (staged/canary, gated on the benchmark) → Monitor (live traces + online evals) → Migrate (re-test + re-baseline on ANY model change) → Deprecate (track the model's Active→Legacy→Deprecated→Retired clock, ≥60 days notice; migrate before retirement). DRIFT: persona/instruction drift is measurable within ~8 conversation turns (attention decay) → keep it small + identity-first AND RELY ON RE-INJECTION (Claude Code re-injects project CLAUDE.md across compaction); treat periodic reinforcement as a REQUIREMENT, not an optimization. MODEL MIGRATION is the headline risk: a persona tuned on one model behaves differently on another and even techniques expire (prefill → 400 on Sonnet 4.6+); PIN a target-model in metadata and re-run the full suite + benchmark before promotion. Model version is part of the persona's compatibility contract.

predicate.spec: the persona is versioned (semver+changelog), pinned to a target-model, re-tested/re-baselined on every model change, periodically re-injected in long runs, and migrated ahead of model retirement.

rules.text: Production reliability comes from the SYSTEM AROUND the persona, not the persona text: specify the output CONTRACT (exact format, verdict vocabulary) so consistency is enforced (use Structured Outputs — note prefill is removed on Sonnet 4.6+); and GUARDRAILS WRAP the agent (input rail → LLM(persona) → output rail) INDEPENDENT of the persona prompt — they don't replace it. Encode the persona's HARD boundaries as guardrail rules in EXTERNAL code (OWASP: 'rely on systems outside of the LLM'). The Claude-Code-native rail is a PreToolUse hook (Anthropic verbatim: 'context, not enforced configuration … use a PreToolUse hook instead'). Genesis GENERATES the enforcement skeleton from the PersonaSpec: interfaces.tools.deny → PreToolUse Bash matcher; boundaries[].never paths → PreToolUse Write/Edit path filter; values leakage rule → output keyword filter; untrusted-content rule → untrusted text only in tool_result, JSON-encoded; escalation.user_owns → human checkpoint (never auto-approved). The persona TELLS the model not to push; the hook makes pushing IMPOSSIBLE — defense in depth, never relying on the persona/model-training alone.

predicate.spec: the persona's hard boundaries (denied tools, protected paths, secrets, escalation) are enforced by external rails (PreToolUse hooks/classifiers/output filters) generated from the spec — not by persona prose alone; the output contract uses Structured Outputs.

rules.text: MONITOR persona adherence in PRODUCTION and handle failures: sample live traces, run the §10 LLM-judge rubric as an ONLINE eval on the sample, and ALERT on any hard-gate metric (boundary-hold, leakage) breaching target or a tracked metric drifting beyond its SE (the benchmark runs continuously on real traffic). Failure sequence when adherence fails: DETECT (output classifier flags out-of-role / boundary-violating / leaking output) → CONTAIN (block the response, route to a human, or return a safe fallback) → RECOVER (reset the working context + re-inject the persona to counter drift) → RECORD (log the case; it becomes a NEW adversarial test). Never let a detected character break reach the user unmodified.

predicate.spec: live traffic is sampled + judged online with alerts on hard-gate/SE breaches; a detected boundary-violation/leak is contained (blocked/human/fallback), recovered (context reset + re-inject), and recorded as a new test — never shipped unmodified.

rules.text: SECURITY — the persona is SOFT, EXTRACTABLE, and OVERRIDABLE (primary-sourced end to end): (1) the system prompt is NOT a secret and WILL leak → put NO secrets/credentials/auth-logic in the persona (S13); (2) ASSIGNING a persona is itself an attack vector (persona-modulation jailbreaks +185× harmful completion; DAN character-override; transfers across models) → character-override attempts are a FIRST-CLASS test case, not an edge case; (3) LONG CONTEXT erodes the persona (many-shot) → classify/modify the prompt BEFORE the model, don't trust the model to 'remember' its character; (4) INJECTION rides in on tool/retrieved content → put untrusted content ONLY in tool_result, JSON-encoded + source-labeled, and enforce LEAST PRIVILEGE. Pair every attack class (modulation/DAN/long-context/indirect-injection/extraction) with a defense AND an adversarial test.

predicate.spec: the persona holds no secrets; character-override + injection + extraction are covered by external classifiers/least-privilege and by adversarial test cases; untrusted content is confined to JSON-encoded tool_result.

rules.text: SCALING across a fleet (Genesis + its built agents): PER-AGENT ISOLATION (own persona, memory store, hooks — one agent's context can't contaminate another); a SHARED guardrail layer (one classifier/rail set, not re-implemented per persona); a CENTRAL registry with per-agent version + target-model pins; FLEET-WIDE adherence monitoring with per-agent scorecards; SHARED acceptance-test infra (every persona TDD'd + regression-gated identically). The persona stays small (every agent pays its cost every turn); the heavy machinery (guardrails, eval harness, registry) is shared infrastructure authored once. THE PER-AGENT BUNDLE Genesis emits: CLAUDE.md (persona, RENDERED from spec, lifecycle frontmatter) + persona.spec.json (source of truth) + persona.tests.json (TDD + regression gate) + .claude/settings.json (PreToolUse rails from spec) + scorecard.baseline.json + CHANGELOG.md. BUNDLE INVARIANTS (tool-checkable, fail the build if violated): (1) CLAUDE.md is byte-identical to a fresh render of persona.spec.json; (2) every ★ spec field has ≥1 case in persona.tests.json; (3) every tools.deny/path boundary has a matching rail in settings.json; (4) target-model in frontmatter equals the model the scorecard baseline was measured on; (5) a version bump touches spec + changelog + re-runs the suite.

predicate.spec: each built agent ships the complete bundle (spec+persona+tests+rails+scorecard+changelog) under per-agent isolation with shared guardrail/registry/eval infra; the 5 bundle invariants hold or the build fails.
